```{r modeling}
# LEGO CASE STUDY: COMPLETE MODELING WORKFLOW
# Base R only; no additional packages required.
# In RStudio, run this script and select case-study2-data (1).csv.
# The split and folds are generated automatically using seed 123.
# R and Python use different random generators: update the report with these R results.

# 1. LOAD AND CLEAN DATA --------------------------------------------------
input_file <- file.choose()
x <- read.csv(input_file, fileEncoding = 'windows-1252',
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c('', 'NA'))
x$row_id <- seq_len(nrow(x))
x$Amazon_Price <- as.numeric(gsub('[$, ]', '', x$Amazon_Price))
age_text <- gsub('\u00bd', '.5', x$Ages)
matched <- grepl('Ages_[0-9]+', age_text)
x$age <- NA_real_
x$age[matched] <- as.numeric(sub('.*Ages_([0-9]+(?:\\.[0-9]+)?).*',
                                '\\1', age_text[matched], perl = TRUE))
d <- x[!is.na(x$Amazon_Price) & x$Amazon_Price > 0 &
       !is.na(x$Pieces) & x$Pieces > 0, ]
stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1304, nrow(d) == 826)
output_dir <- file.path(dirname(input_file), 'LEGO_modeling_results')
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# 2. AUTOMATIC TRAINING/TEST SPLIT ----------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
train_rows <- sample(seq_len(nrow(d)), size = floor(0.80 * nrow(d)))
test_rows <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(d)), train_rows)
train <- d[train_rows, ]
test <- d[test_rows, ]
fold_id <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(train)))
cat('Training sets:', nrow(train), '\nTest sets:', nrow(test), '\n')
print(table(fold_id))

model_names <- c('Raw price: pieces', 'Log price: log pieces',
                 'Log price: structure', 'Log price: theme',
                 'Log price: theme + construction')

# 2. PREPROCESS USING TRAINING DATA ONLY ----------------------------------
# For log models, imputation is on the transformed scale.
# Missing minifigures can indicate zero OR unknown; never replace all by zero.
# Indicators require >=5 missing training observations to avoid singleton fits.
# Pool themes with fewer than 15 training observations into Other.
make_design <- function(a, b, model) {
  A <- matrix(1, nrow(a), 1, dimnames = list(NULL, 'Intercept'))
  B <- matrix(1, nrow(b), 1, dimnames = list(NULL, 'Intercept'))
  columns <- 'Pieces'
  labels <- if (model == 1) 'pieces' else 'log_pieces'
  if (model >= 3) {
    columns <- c(columns, 'Minifigures', 'age')
    labels <- c(labels, 'log1p_minifigures', 'minimum_age')
  }
  if (model == 5) {
    columns <- c(columns, 'Pages', 'Unique_Pieces')
    labels <- c(labels, 'log_pages', 'log_unique_pieces')
  }
  for (j in seq_along(columns)) {
    col <- columns[j]; aa <- a[[col]]; bb <- b[[col]]
    if (model > 1 && col != 'age') {
      aa <- if (col == 'Minifigures') log1p(aa) else log(aa)
      bb <- if (col == 'Minifigures') log1p(bb) else log(bb)
    }
    missing_a <- is.na(aa); missing_b <- is.na(bb)
    med <- median(aa, na.rm = TRUE)
    aa[missing_a] <- med; bb[missing_b] <- med
    A <- cbind(A, aa); B <- cbind(B, bb)
    colnames(A)[ncol(A)] <- colnames(B)[ncol(B)] <- labels[j]
    if (sum(missing_a) >= 5) {
      A <- cbind(A, as.numeric(missing_a)); B <- cbind(B, as.numeric(missing_b))
      colnames(A)[ncol(A)] <- colnames(B)[ncol(B)] <- paste0(labels[j], '_missing')
    }
  }
  cats <- if (model >= 3) 'Year' else character()
  if (model == 3) cats <- c(cats, 'Size')
  if (model >= 4) cats <- c(cats, 'Theme')
  for (col in cats) {
    aa <- as.character(a[[col]]); bb <- as.character(b[[col]])
    aa[is.na(aa)] <- 'Unknown'; bb[is.na(bb)] <- 'Unknown'
    if (col == 'Theme') {
      counts <- table(aa); common <- names(counts[counts >= 15])
      aa[!aa %in% common] <- 'Other'; bb[!bb %in% common] <- 'Other'
    }
    levels <- sort(unique(aa), method = 'radix')
    if (length(levels) > 1) for (lev in levels[-1]) {
      A <- cbind(A, as.numeric(aa == lev)); B <- cbind(B, as.numeric(bb == lev))
      colnames(A)[ncol(A)] <- colnames(B)[ncol(B)] <- paste(col, lev, sep = '_')
    }
  }
  list(A = A, B = B)
}

# 3. FIT AND BACK-TRANSFORM -----------------------------------------------
fit_predict <- function(a, b, model) {
  design <- make_design(a, b, model)
  y <- if (model == 1) a$Amazon_Price else log(a$Amazon_Price)
  fit <- lm.fit(design$A, y)
  if (fit$rank < ncol(design$A)) stop('Rank-deficient design: inspect predictors.')
  smearing <- if (model == 1) 1 else mean(exp(fit$residuals))
  prediction <- drop(design$B %*% fit$coefficients)
  if (model > 1) prediction <- exp(prediction) * smearing
  list(prediction = prediction, fit = fit, A = design$A,
       B = design$B, y = y, smearing = smearing)
}
rmse <- function(y, p) sqrt(mean((y - p)^2))
mae <- function(y, p) mean(abs(y - p))
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# FIX CHARACTER ENCODING ERROR IN LEGO CROSS-VALIDATION
# ============================================================

# 1. Back up the original training data
train_backup <- train

# 2. Identify character variables
char_vars <- names(train)[sapply(train, is.character)]

# 3. Examine original character encodings
for (var in char_vars) {
  cat("\nVariable:", var, "\n")
  print(table(Encoding(train[[var]]), useNA = "ifany"))
}

# 4. Convert character variables to UTF-8
for (var in char_vars) {
  train[[var]] <- iconv(
    train[[var]],
    from = "",
    to = "UTF-8",
    sub = NA
  )
}

# 5. Check whether conversion introduced missing values
for (var in char_vars) {
  new_missing <- sum(is.na(train[[var]]) &
                    !is.na(train_backup[[var]]))

  cat(var, "- New missing values:", new_missing, "\n")
}

# 6. Verify that categorical values can be sorted
for (var in char_vars) {
  cat("\nChecking:", var, "\n")

  result <- try(
    sort(unique(train[[var]])),
    silent = TRUE
  )

  if (inherits(result, "try-error")) {
    cat("Sorting failed:", var, "\n")
  } else {
    cat("Sorting successful\n")
  }
}

# 7. Test the previously failing Model 4, Fold 1
validation <- fold_id == 1

test_result <- try(
  fit_predict(
    train[!validation, ],
    train[validation, ],
    4
  ),
  silent = TRUE
)

# 8. Check if Model 4 works
if (inherits(test_result, "try-error")) {

  cat("\nModel 4 still failed.\n")
  print(test_result)

} else {

  cat("\nModel 4, Fold 1 completed successfully!\n")

  # 9. Run the complete five-fold cross-validation
  comparison <- data.frame(
    Model = model_names,
    CV_RMSE = NA_real_,
    CV_MAE = NA_real_
  )

  for (model in 1:5) {

    predictions <- numeric(nrow(train))

    for (fold in 1:5) {

      cat("Model:", model, "Fold:", fold, "\n")

      validation <- fold_id == fold

      predictions[validation] <- fit_predict(
        train[!validation, ],
        train[validation, ],
        model
      )$prediction
    }

    comparison$CV_RMSE[model] <- rmse(
      train$Amazon_Price,
      predictions
    )

    comparison$CV_MAE[model] <- mae(
      train$Amazon_Price,
      predictions
    )
  }

  # 10. Display model comparison results
  print(comparison)

  # 11. Select model with lowest cross-validation RMSE
  selected <- which.min(comparison$CV_RMSE)

  cat("\nSelected model:", model_names[selected], "\n")
}
```

```{r}
# 5. HELD-OUT EVALUATION --------------------------------------------------
result <- fit_predict(train, test, selected)
pred <- result$prediction
metrics <- data.frame(
  Measure = c('Test RMSE', 'Test MAE', 'Test R-squared', 'Mean baseline RMSE', 'Smearing factor'),
  Value = c(rmse(test$Amazon_Price, pred), mae(test$Amazon_Price, pred),
            1 - sum((test$Amazon_Price - pred)^2) / sum((test$Amazon_Price - mean(test$Amazon_Price))^2),
            rmse(test$Amazon_Price, rep(mean(train$Amazon_Price), nrow(test))), result$smearing))
print(metrics)
write.csv(metrics, file.path(output_dir, 'test_metrics.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
held_out <- data.frame(Item_Number = test$Item_Number, Set_Name = test$Set_Name,
                       Observed = test$Amazon_Price, Predicted = pred,
                       Error = pred - test$Amazon_Price)
write.csv(held_out, file.path(output_dir, 'held_out_predictions.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
print(head(held_out[order(abs(held_out$Error), decreasing = TRUE), ], 5))

# 6. HC3 ROBUST COEFFICIENT INTERVALS --------------------------------------
# Intervals are conditional on the selected model and imputed predictors.
# They do not account for model-selection uncertainty.
A <- result$A; e <- result$fit$residuals; fitted <- result$fit$fitted.values
n <- nrow(A); p <- ncol(A)
bread <- solve(crossprod(A))
h <- rowSums((A %*% bread) * A)
V_HC3 <- bread %*% crossprod(A, A * as.numeric((e / (1 - h))^2)) %*% bread
se <- sqrt(diag(V_HC3)); beta <- result$fit$coefficients
critical <- qt(.975, df = n - p)
coefficients <- data.frame(Term = colnames(A), Estimate = beta, HC3_SE = se,
                           CI_low = beta - critical * se, CI_high = beta + critical * se,
                           p_value = 2 * pt(abs(beta / se), df = n - p, lower.tail = FALSE))
print(coefficients, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(coefficients, file.path(output_dir, 'coefficients.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

# 7. DIAGNOSTICS AND INFLUENCE --------------------------------------------
# Studentized Breusch-Pagan LM statistic (same default as statsmodels).
aux <- lm.fit(A, e^2)
aux_r2 <- 1 - sum(aux$residuals^2) / sum((e^2 - mean(e^2))^2)
bp_stat <- n * aux_r2
cat('\nBreusch-Pagan p-value:', pchisq(bp_stat, p - 1, lower.tail = FALSE), '\n')
mse <- sum(e^2) / (n - p)
cooks <- e^2 / (p * mse) * h / (1 - h)^2
largest <- which.max(cooks)
cat('Largest Cook distance:', max(cooks), '\nSet:', train$Set_Name[largest], '\n')
# Sensitivity only: do NOT remove the observation from the primary results.
sensitivity <- fit_predict(train[-largest, ], test, selected)
cat('Sensitivity RMSE excluding this training observation:',
    rmse(test$Amazon_Price, sensitivity$prediction), '\n')

# 8. SAVE COLORLESS GRAPHS ------------------------------------------------
png(file.path(output_dir, 'model_comparison.png'), width = 1800, height = 1000, res = 200)
par(mar = c(5, 15, 2, 1))
barplot(rev(comparison$CV_RMSE), names.arg = rev(model_names), horiz = TRUE,
        las = 1, col = 'white', border = 'black',
        xlab = 'Training cross-validation RMSE ($)')
dev.off()
png(file.path(output_dir, 'predictions.png'), width = 1400, height = 1200, res = 200)
limits <- range(c(0, test$Amazon_Price, pred))
plot(test$Amazon_Price, pred, pch = 1, xlim = limits, ylim = limits,
     xlab = 'Observed Amazon price ($)', ylab = 'Predicted Amazon price ($)',
     main = 'Held-out predictions')
abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
dev.off()
png(file.path(output_dir, 'diagnostics.png'), width = 2000, height = 900, res = 200)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(fitted, e, pch = 1, xlab = 'Fitted log price', ylab = 'Residual',
     main = 'Training residuals')
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
qqnorm(e, pch = 1, main = 'Normal Q-Q plot'); qqline(e, col = 'black')
dev.off()
png(file.path(output_dir, 'cooks_distance.png'), width = 1600, height = 1000, res = 200)
plot(cooks, type = 'h', xlab = 'Training observation', ylab = "Cook's distance",
     main = 'Influence diagnostics')
abline(h = 4/n, lty = 2)
dev.off()

# 9. RECORD REPRODUCIBILITY DETAILS ---------------------------------------
write.csv(data.frame(row_id = train$row_id, fold = fold_id),
          file.path(output_dir, 'training_split.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(row_id = test$row_id), file.path(output_dir, 'test_split.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(output_dir, 'R_session_info.txt'))
cat('\nAll results saved in:', output_dir, '\n')
# Do not repeatedly tune models using these test results.
# The 2018-2020 data do not validate predictions for today's market.
```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# MODEL 6: RIDGE REGRESSION
# Nested 5-fold CV; original test set remains untouched
# ============================================================

if (!requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("glmnet")
}
library(glmnet)

# Candidate penalty values
lambda_grid <- 10^seq(-2, 3, length.out = 50)

# Fit Ridge and predict at multiple lambda values
ridge_predictions <- function(a, b, lambdas) {

  # Same predictors and preprocessing as Model 4
  design <- make_design(a, b, 4)

  X_train <- design$A[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  X_new <- design$B[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  y_train <- log(a$Amazon_Price)

  ridge_fit <- glmnet(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    alpha = 0,
    lambda = lambdas,
    standardize = TRUE
  )

  # Predictions on log scale
  log_train <- as.matrix(predict(
    ridge_fit, newx = X_train, s = lambdas
  ))
  log_new <- as.matrix(predict(
    ridge_fit, newx = X_new, s = lambdas
  ))

  # Training-only smearing factors, one per lambda
  smear <- colMeans(exp(
    sweep(log_train, 1, y_train, FUN = "-") * -1
  ))

  # Back-transform to original dollar scale
  prediction <- sweep(exp(log_new), 2, smear, "*")

  prediction
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Inner CV: choose lambda using dollar-scale RMSE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

tune_ridge <- function(a, lambdas, seed = 123) {

  set.seed(seed)
  inner_fold <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(a)))

  squared_error <- numeric(length(lambdas))

  for (k in 1:5) {

    val <- inner_fold == k

    prediction <- ridge_predictions(
      a[!val, ],
      a[val, ],
      lambdas
    )

    errors <- sweep(
      prediction, 1, a$Amazon_Price[val], "-"
    )

    squared_error <- squared_error +
      colSums(errors^2)
  }

  cv_rmse <- sqrt(squared_error / nrow(a))

  list(
    best_lambda = lambdas[which.min(cv_rmse)],
    cv_rmse = cv_rmse
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Outer CV: evaluate Ridge using original folds
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ridge_oof <- numeric(nrow(train))
ridge_lambdas <- numeric(5)

for (fold in 1:5) {

  validation <- fold_id == fold

  outer_train <- train[!validation, ]
  outer_validation <- train[validation, ]

  tuned <- tune_ridge(
    outer_train,
    lambda_grid,
    seed = 123 + fold
  )

  ridge_lambdas[fold] <- tuned$best_lambda

  ridge_oof[validation] <- drop(ridge_predictions(
    outer_train,
    outer_validation,
    tuned$best_lambda
  ))

  cat("Outer fold:", fold,
      "Selected lambda:", tuned$best_lambda, "\n")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Compare Model 6 with Model 4
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ridge_rmse <- rmse(train$Amazon_Price, ridge_oof)
ridge_mae <- mae(train$Amazon_Price, ridge_oof)

ridge_comparison <- rbind(
  comparison[4, ],
  data.frame(
    Model = "Ridge: log price + theme",
    CV_RMSE = ridge_rmse,
    CV_MAE = ridge_mae
  )
)

print(ridge_comparison)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Tune Ridge on all training observations
# Do not use the test data to select lambda
# ------------------------------------------------------------

final_tuning <- tune_ridge(
  train,
  lambda_grid,
  seed = 456
)

cat("Final Ridge lambda:",
    final_tuning$best_lambda, "\n")

# Save cross-validation comparison
write.csv(
  ridge_comparison,
  file.path(output_dir, "ridge_comparison.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# MODEL 7: LASSO REGRESSION
# Nested five-fold cross-validation
# ============================================================

library(glmnet)

# 1. Candidate lambda values
lambda_grid_lasso <- c(
  0,
  10^seq(-5, 3, length.out = 100)
)

# 2. Fit LASSO and predict on the dollar scale
lasso_predictions <- function(a, b, lambdas) {

  # Same predictors as Model 4
  design <- make_design(a, b, 4)

  X_train <- design$A[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  X_new <- design$B[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  y_train <- log(a$Amazon_Price)

  # L1 regularization
  fit <- glmnet(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    alpha = 1,
    lambda = lambdas,
    standardize = TRUE
  )

  # Predict training and validation log-prices
  log_train <- as.matrix(
    predict(fit, newx = X_train, s = lambdas)
  )

  log_new <- as.matrix(
    predict(fit, newx = X_new, s = lambdas)
  )

  # Smearing correction based on fitting observations
  smear <- colMeans(
    exp(sweep(log_train, 1, y_train, FUN = "-") * -1)
  )

  # Convert predictions to dollars
  predictions <- sweep(exp(log_new), 2, smear, "*")

  predictions
}

# 3. Tune lambda using five-fold inner CV
tune_lasso <- function(a, lambdas, seed = 123) {

  set.seed(seed)
  inner_fold <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(a)))

  squared_error <- numeric(length(lambdas))

  for (k in 1:5) {

    val <- inner_fold == k

    predictions <- lasso_predictions(
      a[!val, ],
      a[val, ],
      lambdas
    )

    errors <- sweep(
      predictions, 1, a$Amazon_Price[val], "-"
    )

    squared_error <- squared_error + colSums(errors^2)
  }

  cv_rmse <- sqrt(squared_error / nrow(a))

  list(
    best_lambda = lambdas[which.min(cv_rmse)],
    cv_rmse = cv_rmse
  )
}

# 4. Outer CV: obtain out-of-fold predictions
lasso_oof <- numeric(nrow(train))
lasso_lambdas <- numeric(5)

for (fold in 1:5) {

  validation <- fold_id == fold

  outer_train <- train[!validation, ]
  outer_validation <- train[validation, ]

  tuned <- tune_lasso(
    outer_train,
    lambda_grid_lasso,
    seed = 123 + fold
  )

  lasso_lambdas[fold] <- tuned$best_lambda

  lasso_oof[validation] <- drop(lasso_predictions(
    outer_train,
    outer_validation,
    tuned$best_lambda
  ))

  cat("Outer fold:", fold,
      "Selected lambda:", tuned$best_lambda, "\n")
}

# 5. Cross-validation metrics
lasso_rmse <- rmse(train$Amazon_Price, lasso_oof)
lasso_mae <- mae(train$Amazon_Price, lasso_oof)

# 6. Compare OLS, Ridge, and LASSO
lasso_comparison <- rbind(
  ridge_comparison,
  data.frame(
    Model = "LASSO: log price + theme",
    CV_RMSE = lasso_rmse,
    CV_MAE = lasso_mae
  )
)

print(lasso_comparison)

# 7. Tune final lambda using training data only
final_lasso_tuning <- tune_lasso(
  train,
  lambda_grid_lasso,
  seed = 456
)

best_lasso_lambda <- final_lasso_tuning$best_lambda

cat("Final LASSO lambda:", best_lasso_lambda, "\n")

# 8. Fit final LASSO and identify selected predictors
design <- make_design(train, train, 4)

X <- design$A[, -1, drop = FALSE]

final_lasso <- glmnet(
  x = X,
  y = log(train$Amazon_Price),
  alpha = 1,
  lambda = best_lasso_lambda,
  standardize = TRUE
)

lasso_coef <- as.matrix(coef(final_lasso))

selected_predictors <- data.frame(
  Predictor = rownames(lasso_coef),
  Coefficient = as.numeric(lasso_coef[, 1])
)

selected_predictors <- selected_predictors[
  selected_predictors$Coefficient != 0 &
  selected_predictors$Predictor != "(Intercept)",
]

cat("\nNumber of selected predictors:",
    nrow(selected_predictors), "\n")

print(selected_predictors)

# 9. Save results
write.csv(
  lasso_comparison,
  file.path(output_dir, "lasso_comparison.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  selected_predictors,
  file.path(output_dir, "lasso_selected_predictors.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

```{r}
# Graph 2: Zoomed-in view
plot(
  observed, predicted,
  pch = 16,
  col = "gray50",
  xlim = c(0, 200),
  ylim = c(0, 200),
  xlab = "Observed Amazon Price ($)",
  ylab = "Predicted Amazon Price ($)",
  main = "Ridge: Observed vs. Predicted Prices (Zoomed)"
)

abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "black")

```



```{r}

# Count total, retained, and eliminated coefficients

total_predictors <- ncol(X)

retained_predictors <- nrow(selected_predictors)

removed_predictors <- total_predictors - retained_predictors

selection_summary <- data.frame(
  Measure = c(
    "Total predictor coefficients",
    "Retained coefficients",
    "Eliminated coefficients",
    "Percentage eliminated"
  ),
  Value = c(
    total_predictors,
    retained_predictors,
    removed_predictors,
    round(100 * removed_predictors / total_predictors, 2)
  )
)

print(selection_summary)

```

```{r}

# Selection stability across five outer training folds
library(glmnet)

selection_list <- vector("list", 5)

for (fold in 1:5) {

  validation <- fold_id == fold

  fold_train <- train[!validation, ]

  design_fold <- make_design(
    fold_train, fold_train, 4
  )

  X_fold <- design_fold$A[, -1, drop = FALSE]

  fit_fold <- glmnet(
    x = X_fold,
    y = log(fold_train$Amazon_Price),
    alpha = 1,
    lambda = lasso_lambdas[fold],
    standardize = TRUE
  )

  coefs <- as.matrix(coef(fit_fold))

  selected <- rownames(coefs)[
    as.numeric(coefs[, 1]) != 0
  ]

  selection_list[[fold]] <- setdiff(
    selected, "(Intercept)"
  )
}

# Count how often each predictor was selected
all_predictors <- sort(unique(
  unlist(selection_list)
))

selection_frequency <- sapply(
  all_predictors,
  function(v) {
    sum(sapply(selection_list, function(s) v %in% s))
  }
)

stability_table <- data.frame(
  Predictor = all_predictors,
  Folds_Selected = as.integer(selection_frequency),
  Selection_Percentage = 100 * selection_frequency / 5
)

stability_table <- stability_table[
  order(-stability_table$Folds_Selected),
]

print(stability_table)

write.csv(
  stability_table,
  file.path(output_dir, "lasso_selection_stability.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```
